body:
Triage: lands in `plugin-security` / default permission sets if B or C is taken, checklist prose only if A ⇒ `domain:identity`; type **Feature** (B/C widen a read admission beyond what #8095 ruled — accept-set expansion routes to the human floor). ⇒ `needs-user-decision`: even taking A decides a permission boundary ("`delegated_admin` shall not read the ledger"), which is not auto-adjudicable.

**Recommendation: A now, with C as the named reopen trigger.**

- **Platform long-term coherence:** A keeps #8095's ruling as the single statement of `sys_invitation` read admission; B widens the ledger's audience by a role the ruling deliberately did not include; C is the most D8-faithful widening but adds a third policy for one persona.
- **Measured business pull:** zero today — the only thing that noticed is the QA checklist wording; no user workflow reads the ledger as `delegated_admin`. (`docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/identity-auth.json` steps get re-phrased to read as owner/admin under A.)
- **AI-agent error-resistance:** A changes prose only. C's `inviter_id == current_user.id` row scope is a new predicate shape on the policy surface agents must reason about — cheap, but not free (see #8241 for how policy composition on this exact object already bit once).
- **Startup scope discipline:** remove/defer over declare-and-maintain. Reopen trigger for C: a real delegated-admin workflow (UI page or API consumer) that needs to track issued invitations.

If A is taken, the residue is a small Task (checklist re-phrase) that can go straight to `pm:queue`.

## Maintainer ruling — Option C

Ruled by the maintainer in a live PM session, 2026-08-13 (session `session_015XyMgCSMGGn9oSwbQEeWYg`), verbatim: 「其他全部接受你的建议。」 — accepting option C as recommended.

**Ruling: C — a `delegated_admin` sees the invitations they themselves issued** (`inviter_id == current_user.id`), not the whole ledger. This matches ADR-0105 D8's scope-bounded issuance shape: the issuing principal can confirm and review its own work without widening the ledger's audience beyond what #8095 ruled (B rejected for exactly that widening; A rejected because an issuer that cannot even confirm its own issuance is a broken shape).

**Implementation notes for dispatch:**
- One additional row-scope policy on `sys_invitation`, same declarative pattern as the addressee carve-out that #8095 already shipped. Owner/admin visibility unchanged.
- Pleasant consequence, verify it in coverage: the ADR-0105 D8 checklist steps ("as the delegated_admin ... capture the created sys_invitation row via the data API") become correct again as written — no checklist rewording needed. Pin the four-persona matrix from this card's measurement with `delegated_admin` now seeing exactly their own rows.

Label swap: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`.

## Claim — implementing the ruled Option C

- **Session:** `session_01PEVB6w7D7uCszR9Mw1BL73`
- **Branch:** `claude/issue-8240-delegated-admin-own-invitations`
- **Base:** `origin/main` @ `884091c19`

Comments re-read before starting; no prior claim comment from another session on this issue.

**Declared file surface** (plugin-security only — the row-scope policy layer):

- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts`
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.test.ts` (or a sibling test file)
- `.changeset/*.md`

**Disjointness verified against the three in-flight cards** (measured from their live worktrees, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD`, not assumed):

| Card | Its surface | Overlap with mine |
|:--|:--|:--|
| #8317 (`sys_member` role normalisation) | `plugin-auth/src/{auth-plugin,index,member-role-canonical}.ts` | none |
| #8243 (impersonation bearer rotation) | `plugin-auth` hooks + `runtime/src/security/resolve-session-principal.ts` | none |
| #8119 (`plugin-sharing` phantom-anchor mint) | `plugin-sharing/**` | none |

Note on #8317 specifically, since it is the nearest neighbour: its canonicalisation is per-token trim + lower-case against the ADR-0108 closed vocabulary, and `delegated_admin` is already in that vocabulary — so it normalises to `delegated_admin` unchanged, and the position name this card's policy domains on is stable under that card landing either before or after mine.

One non-defect observation, recorded here rather than as an issue because it is standard pnpm semantics and not a repo bug — `pnpm --filter PKG test -- PATTERN` forwards the `--` literally, so the pattern reaches vitest as an argument after `--` and is ignored; the whole suite runs while appearing to be filtered. `pnpm --filter PKG exec vitest run PATH` is the form that actually targets one file.
